title: Engineering Graphics and Design
description: This course develops graphical visualization and design skills by applying graphics based engineering methods. The course also teaches engineering design by applying the conceptual design process and integrating graphics into design projects. Graphics assignments develop sketching, manual drafting, and computer aided drafting (CAD) skills. This course is primarily for engineering transfer students.
outcomes: Construct two-dimensional and three-dimensional drawings of engineering designs using sketching, manual drafting, and computer-aided drafting approaches.
Demonstrate design solutions by presenting team solutions
Synthesize ideas from diverse disciplines to produce creative design solutions of engineering problems using the concepts of the  parametric design process.
objectives: Apply the engineering design process to develop creative solutions to engineering problems.
Apply advanced graphics topics such as descriptive geometry and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing.
Communicate engineering design solutions through verbal presentations and written design reports.
Apply team building skills to develop engineering design solutions.
Apply computer aided graphics techniques to construct engineering designs.
Develop the ability to evaluate engineering drawings and their application to design and fabrication.
Use engineering graphics techniques to communicate technical ideas and solutions.
assignments: A major part of the class is learning how to apply engineering graphics techniques to engineering design problems. Technical language must be learned
and used effectively, including various symbols and views of objects, as a universal language for engineering. Students deliver comprehensive design reports
for three different design projects. Each report identifies the design issues and requirements, illustrate the application of the design process, present the design
solutions, and evaluate the final design.
A typical design project report may be the following: "Design a device that allows you to dig a trench of specified size using only one arm."
Project and drawing assignments are completed both during lab time and at home. A significant amount of out-of-class work is anticipated. Most of the
design projects are completed in groups. It is expected that these groups meet outside of class.
A typical drawing assignment may be the following: "Given the following three
orthogonal views of the clevis bracket, sketch an isometric drawing."
The various steps of the engineering design process itself are excellent examples of critical thinking. The students use graphics tools and apply them to practical
use in designing engineering solutions to problems. The process of correctly and succinctly defining a problem requires critical thinking. Once the problem is
defined, students apply the engineering design process: a multi-step process that includes the analysis of the problem, the development and evaluation of
solutions, decision-making with various alternatives, synthesizing the workable solution, and communicating the solution.
A typical problem involving the design process may be the following: "Apply the design process learned in class to develop and construct a solution for
transferring radioactive objects from one location to another."
